title: Transfer learning for early neuroinflammation detection from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts
abstract: We evaluate a transfer-learning workflow for identifying early neuroinflammation signatures from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts. The approach combines quality-control notebooks, graph-based clustering, and biomarker ranking to improve reproducibility across three public datasets.
introduction: Early detection of neuroinflammation remains difficult because cohorts vary by protocol, sequencing depth, and annotation standards. We test whether a reusable transfer-learning workflow can improve cross-cohort signal detection.
methods: We used Python, Scanpy, and PyTorch to normalize three open single-cell RNA-seq datasets. Models were trained on two cohorts and tested on the third. A preregistered notebook records preprocessing, clustering, and biomarker ranking steps.
results: The model improved F1 from 0.71 to 0.82 compared with a baseline logistic model. The reported p-value was p = 0.031 for the main comparison, but confidence intervals are not currently included. The top biomarkers were validated against external literature.
dataAvailability: Processed matrices and notebooks are planned for release after de-identification review.
